Part 3 – Anchoring and Beaching

What are THREE factors you would consider when selecting an anchorage?

Depth; bottom composition; swing room; changes in tide and weather; ease of moving in case of inclement weather



Select the anchor when anchoring on a soft mud seabed (circle your answers)





 What are TWO ways you can check whether an anchor is dragging?

Reset anchor; use different type of anchor; lay out second anchor; seek more sheltered anchorage or one with different bottom composition, increase scope

What are TWO emergencies that might lead to you beaching a vessel?

Vessel flooding, offload injured persons, fire damage, NUC

What are THREE considerations for re-floating a beached vessel?

Ensure tide suitable, inspect hull for damage, check bilges, remove water or items adding to weight of vessel, brief crew on process, check weather conditions, determine if support vessel is required, ensure bilge systems and safety equipment are in working order, secure loose items





Part 4 – Pre-start checks/Voyage Planning and Refuelling



What would you do if any equipment required on your vessel by NSCV is not functioning?
When would you report a fuel spill to authorities?

Asap once spill is controlled or contained, then be prepared to follow instructions



What are three precautions that will help to reduce the risk of a spill when refuelling?

Smoking, talking on the phone, welding, grinding, hot work, anything likely to cause ignition



In the event of a spill while refuelling, what procedures should you follow?

Vessel SMS procedures -Shut down fuelling system; prevent further spillage, fire-fighting equipment available, contain using spill kit and bunding, alert personnel; alert authorities; clean up any spillage aboard

Check fuel connection

Ensure prop and leg not restricted or damaged

Check oil level (mix and sump as applicable)

Cooling system-water transfer

Spark plug and timing
